objective: Troubleshoot a service that fails to start from its status and journal
secondaryObjectives: Start, stop, restart, enable and disable services with systemctl
Read service logs with journalctl filtered by unit, boot, priority and time

sources.note: Relevant text: systemctl status shows a unit's state and its most recent journal lines; enable creates the symlinks that start a unit at boot and --now also starts it; is-enabled reports it. journalctl -u selects a unit's messages. Read in full 2026-11-14.

sources.cite: nginx Beginner's Guide (configuration file structure) and Command-line parameters (nginx.org)
sources.note: Relevant text: Beginner's Guide, 'A simple directive consists of the name and parameters separated by spaces and ends with a semicolon'; Command-line parameters (nginx.org/en/docs/switches.html), '-t — test the configuration file: nginx checks the configuration for correct syntax'. Both read 2026-11-14. The [emerg] message layout, with file and line, is authored in nginx's style.

Relevant text: dpkg keeps a locally modified configuration file (a conffile) on reinstall or upgrade unless told otherwise, so reinstalling the package does not replace an edited site file. Read in full 2026-11-14 (the --force-conf* options section).

brief.situation: You look after shop1, the web server for Sumner Florist (fictional). At 08:55 a colleague edited the shop's nginx site file to add caching for images and ran systemctl restart nginx; it failed, and the shop has been offline since. Morning delivery orders close at 09:45. The server is also patched and rebooted tonight at 23:00. Get the shop back, and make sure it stays up after the reboot.
handover: The site file is /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/shop; nothing else changed this morning.
This is a Debian server; nginx came from the distribution's package.
howItWorks: Run commands from the command line: type one, or pick it from the suggestions or the action list. Only this lab's commands run; there is no free shell, and each command's arguments are fixed.
Each command takes operator time: run it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The outage keeps developing on the same clock.
The map shows each host, disk or service and the links between them, with a status in words. Output appears in the terminal as it happens.
When you declare the service restored, you write the incident record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the outage record: why nginx would not start, how you found it, and what you did so it also survives tonight's reboot.

parts.label: Cause
parts.criteria: Names the missing semicolon on line 28 of the shop site file: nginx failed its configuration test at start, so systemd marked the unit failed.
parts.modelAnswer: The image-caching edit left root /srv/shop without its semicolon; nginx read on to the closing brace, reported unexpected "}" at line 31 and refused to start.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Uses systemctl status or journalctl -u nginx, and nginx -t, before changing anything; does not blame the package or the port.
parts.modelAnswer: journalctl -u nginx showed the [emerg] line with the file and line; nginx -t repeated it; the lines above 31 showed the missing semicolon.

parts.label: Fix
parts.criteria: Restores the semicolon, runs nginx -t until it passes, then restarts, enables nginx at boot and checks the shop answers; never removes the site or relies on a reinstall.
parts.modelAnswer: Fixed line 28, nginx -t passed, systemctl restart nginx, systemctl enable nginx (it was disabled, so tonight's reboot would have taken the shop down again), and curl returned the shop's 200.

expertPath.text: systemctl status nginx and journalctl -u nginx: [emerg] unexpected "}" at line 31; the unit is also disabled.
Look at the lines above 31: root /srv/shop has no semicolon.
Fix line 28, nginx -t passes, systemctl restart nginx, systemctl enable nginx.
curl the shop for a 200; record the cause and suggest nginx -t before every reload.

scoring.modelReasoning: A service that fails right after a config edit: read systemctl status and journalctl -u nginx, which name the file and line; nginx -t confirms. Restore the missing semicolon, run nginx -t until it passes, restart, enable the unit (it was disabled, so tonight's reboot would take the shop down), and curl the shop.
